content:
anya: New hire hit tsc error in Worker starter: 'No overload matches this call' on chat. Wranger dev runs fine.

sam: Are they using default import? That often causes issues with ESM/CJS resolution.

anya: Yes: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` then `await Redwood.chat({...})`. tsconfig: module=esnext, isolatedModules=true, no esModuleInterop.

lee: Classic. Default import + conditional exports can make TS pick the wrong overload and fall back to unknown. Recommend switching sample to the ESM-friendly surface: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = createClient()`

carla: Also add a tiny helper in samples that narrows the response when inference fails: `export async function chatText(...) { const r = await client.chat(...) as ChatResponse; return r.choices[0].message.content }`. Ugly but helps onboarding.

sam: Also document explicit generics: `await client.chat<ChatResponse>({...})` and a short tsconfig note for edge runtimes (isolatedModules users).

lee: For Cloudflare specifically, ensure package.json has an `import` condition and that `types` point to ESM typings. As a temporary workaround the sample can import `@redwood/inference/esm`.

anya: I'll open a PR to update the worker starter + README with a new "Edge TS tips" section and add a CI check: `tsc --noEmit` with isolatedModules for samples.

ci-bot: job queued: samples/worker/ts-isolatedmodules-check (esbuild matrix).

carla: One more: keep `unknown` in core types for safety. Provide small helper types/utilities for DX (e.g., `parseMessage<T>(m: unknown): T`) and document when to use `as`.

anya: thanks all 44d will link PR shortly and close once CI green.
